identity.name: Kingdom of Linjiang (Eighteen Kingdoms)
alt_names: Kingdom of Linjiang under Gong Ao and Gong Wei

land.text: Nan Commandery and the lands to the south, formerly Qin's

predecessors.note: The Gong Ao page: 'Gong Ao's fief was located in Nan Commandery', most of present-day northern Hubei; the Eighteen Kingdoms table adds northern Hunan.

land.text: the kingdom conquered by Liu Bang's forces in 202

successors.note: Timeline of the Chu-Han Contention, 202 BC: 'Liu Bang's forces conquer the Kingdom of Linjiang and execute its king, Gong Wei.' Cliopatria's Western Chu shape of 203 overlaps about half of this outline (see notes).

capitals.name: Jiangling (Jingzhou, Hubei)
capitals.note: 'Jiangling (江陵; present-day Jiangling County, Jingzhou, Hubei) as his capital'. Jiangling is not in places.jsonl; Jingzhou (112.23, 30.32) is.

rulers.name: Gong Ao
rulers.note: 'granted Gong Ao the title of King of Linjiang'; 'Gong Ao died in 204 BC and was succeeded by his son Gong Wei.'

rulers.name: Gong Wei
rulers.note: Executed in 202 when Liu Bang's forces conquered the kingdom.

keyframe_review.note: 216,393 km2 for 206-204, bbox 108.7-116.0 E, 29.0-33.8 N: the table's 'western Hubei, northern Hunan'. No page gives an area, so no infobox figure to compare. The Gong Ao page puts the fief in Nan Commandery (most of present-day northern Hubei), which is smaller than the table's; the shape follows the table. The row stops in 204 but the kingdom lasts to 202 (new keyframe).

correction.text: unchanged outline carried forward to the kingdom's conquest in 202

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Linjiang after 204, but the Timeline page keeps the kingdom, under Gong Wei, until Liu Bang's forces conquer it in 202. Cliopatria's Western Chu row for 203 contains about half of this outline (western-chu dossier: 'page silent on Gong Wei and Linjiang'); the compiler must choose, and this dossier's page says Linjiang still stood. Reviewer 2026-10-19 (polygon test): Cliopatria's Han row for 203 (kingdom-of-han's han_-203) also covers about 43 percent of this outline and Western Chu's 203 shape about 47 percent, so about nine tenths of Linjiang is claimed by one of the two in 203.

region.text: western Hubei and northern Hunan (Eighteen Kingdoms table); the fief 'located in Nan Commandery' (Gong Ao page)

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Gong Ao King of Linjiang at Jiangling. 'After the fall of Qin in 206 BC, Xiang Yu divided the former Qin Empire' and 'granted Gong Ao the title of King of Linjiang'; 'Gong Ao's fief was located in Nan Commandery'. The Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Linjiang (臨江) ... Gong Ao (Chu general); western Hubei, northern Hunan'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Linjiang, conquered with the execution of Gong Wei

ledger.note: 202: Liu Bang's forces conquer Linjiang. 'Liu Bang's forces conquer the Kingdom of Linjiang and execute its king, Gong Wei.' (Gong Ao had died in 204 and was succeeded by his son Gong Wei.) The Timeline page gives no month.
202: the Kingdom of Linjiang ends with the execution of its king Gong Wei; Liu Bang became emperor of the Han in 202 BCE (Eighteen Kingdoms page).

wars.name: Chu-Han Contention

zones.text: the Kingdom of Linjiang, conquered by Liu Bang's forces in 202

wars.outcome: Han victory (infobox '206-202 BCE'). Linjiang stood on Xiang Yu's side ('although Gong Ao was on Xiang Yu's side, he did not participate in the conflict') and was conquered in 202.
wars.note: The Chu-Han Contention page does not mention Linjiang; the Timeline page supplies 204 (Gong Ao dies) and 202 (conquest). Which Han force took it is not on the pages opened.

certainty.note: The kingdom was assigned by Xiang Yu from commanderies; no survey or treaty lines. The northern and eastern limits (against Hán, Jiujiang and Western Chu) are Cliopatria's approximation.

notes:
Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve Cliopatria rows; Linjiang is its own kingdom with its own kings (Gong Ao, Gong Wei), so it keeps its own dossier.
The kingdom outlives the Cliopatria row (ends 204) by two years on the Timeline page's evidence (202); the Western Chu row of 203 (354,000 km2) contains about half of the Linjiang outline in Cliopatria and the western-chu dossier found its page silent, so the two dossiers now both claim those cells for 203-202. Whoever compiles must choose; no page opened says Western Chu held Linjiang. The han-dynasty dossier (another part) should carry the matching gain in 202 and the kingdom-of-han/han-dynasty dossiers have no entry for it yet.
Page budget: the Eighteen Kingdoms, Gong Ao and Timeline pages were all that said anything dated; the Chu-Han Contention page is silent on Linjiang. The Gong Ao page's 'late 206 BC' secret order to kill Emperor Yi differs from the Xiang Yu page's 205 for Ying Bu's murder of him; neither moves a border.
